title: Law enforcement meets the unknown with UAP-PD
excerpt: Retired Arizona police officers Marianne Robb and Dave Rich are presenting their findings on the challenges of investigating unidentified anomalous phenomena and the reasons why first responders often stay silent about such experiences.
content:
John Forest

Updated Fri, November 20, 2026 at 4:02 AM UTC

LAS VEGAS (KLAS) - Almost a decade ago, in 2017, a high school in Arizona received a mysterious 911 call from what sounded like a frightened young girl.

"I'm scared," she whispered.

Police searched the campus and found nobody there, though numerous unexplained incidents occurred.

This case inspired the creation of UAP-PD, an organization for police officers and first responders who have witnessed unexplained events, according to founders Marianne Robb & Dave Rich.

Robb and Rich are both retired Arizona police officers with six decades of law enforcement experience between them. They take investigations into Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP), the paranormal, and cryptids seriously, helping other officers despite the challenges that have historically hindered UAP and paranormal investigations within police circles. The duo explores unexplained sightings, whether seen in the sky or on land.

They continue to run up against a disheartening truth: while performing their duties, some dedicated law enforcement officers and first responders have witnessed perplexing phenomena and chose to remain silent about their experiences.

That is where the UAP-PD steps in. Their mission is not to prove UFOs or ghosts exist, but to provide a confidential place for officers to discuss experiences without risking the personal and professional risks that come with public disclosure.

So far, the duo has investigated over 100 cases of such phenomena, conducting a thorough investigation of each. For law enforcement officials who would like to reach out directly to the group, anonymous tips can be submitted here.
